### Observed differences

- The activities A34, A35, A36 and A37 now occur in almost every case: participation rose from about 61 in 100 traces to all 200 for A34 and A35, and from about 40 in 100 to about 99 in 100 for A36 and A37 (79 → 198 traces). [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- These four activities are now sequentially linked: before, A34/A35 and A36/A37 almost never appeared in the same trace (co-occurrence about 1 in 200, each side usually excluding the other); in the later window they co-occur in about 99 in 100 traces, with A34/A35 before A36/A37 in about 98–99 in 100. A36 and A37 also now co-occur in about 99 in 100 traces, up from about 40 in 100. [REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- A30 now precedes A34/A35 in about 99 in 100 traces (before about 60 in 100) and precedes A36/A37 in about 98 in 100 (before about 39 in 100); A30's outgoing transitions now go almost exclusively to A35 (about 53 in 100) and A34 (about 46 in 100), whereas before A36 and A37 also received about 17 and 21 in 100. [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, DIR004]
- A31 now comes later: before, about 56% of A34's and 42% of A35's outgoing transitions led directly to A31 at a distance of 1–2 steps; after, these shares drop to under 1%, A31 follows A34/A35 at 3–4 steps (A34 before A31 in 99 in 100 traces, A36/A37 before A31 in about 98 in 100), and the A30→A31 distance moves from about 3 steps to 5. [DIR005, DIR006, LAG008, LAG009, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, LAG005]
- A15 and A16 now precede this block in essentially every trace: co-occurrence of A15 or A16 with A34/A35 rose from about 61 to 100 in 100, and with A36/A37 from about 40 to 99 in 100, with A15/A16 first. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- A06 appears in about 28 in 100 traces in the later window, up from about 7 in 100 (13 → 57 traces), at an earlier position (median relative position about 0.31 → 0.21); about 90 in 100 of its outgoing transitions now go to A16, typically one step away, where before they were spread over many activities. A06 now precedes A30, A31 and A34–A37 in about 26 in 100 traces (before about 2–5 in 100), and A15 routes to A06 in about 15% of its transitions, up from under 1%. [OCC001, POS001, DIR002, LAG001, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, DIR003]
- A10 participation fell from about 10 in 100 traces to about 3 in 100 (20 → 5 traces), and A02's outgoing mix changed almost completely, though the latter rests on only 17 versus 10 observed outgoing transitions. [OCC002, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the process executes a fixed block A30 → A34/A35 → A36/A37 in essentially every case, with A31 postponed to after A36/A37 (3–5 steps downstream) instead of following A34/A35 directly, and that an A06 step leading to A16 is inserted earlier in about 28 in 100 cases, while A10 is executed far less often. The ordering claims rest on direct relational, routing and distance evidence, not on frequency shifts alone, and the two main differences (the A30–A37/A31 block and the A06 insertion), plus the A10 decline, clearly exceed the roughly 0.76 items expected by chance among the 152 tested units. [REL017, REL026, DIR005, LAG008, OCC001, DIR002, REL003, OCC002]

Limitations: the two windows are finite samples of 200 traces each, so a shift in the mix of executed variants — an existing path now run in all cases rather than a modified process — would produce the same pattern and cannot be ruled out; the before-profile of A06 rests on only 13 traces (and 14 outgoing transitions) and the A10 decline on only 5 later traces. Items sharing the same activities (participation, order and distance for the A30–A37 block) describe the same traces and are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002]
